From fe6653460ee7a7dbe0cd5fd322992af862ce5ab0 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Pan Bian <bianpan2016@163.com>
Date: Thu, 21 Jan 2021 01:18:47 -0800
Subject: [PATCH] mtd: spi-nor: hisi-sfc: Put child node np on error path

Put the child node np when it fails to get or register device.

Fixes: e523f11141bd ("mtd: spi-nor: add hisilicon spi-nor flash controller driver")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Pan Bian <bianpan2016@163.com>
[ta: Add Fixes tag and Cc stable]
Signed-off-by: Tudor Ambarus <tudor.ambarus@microchip.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20210121091847.85362-1-bianpan2016@163.com

diff --git a/drivers/mtd/spi-nor/controllers/hisi-sfc.c b/drivers/mtd/spi-nor/controllers/hisi-sfc.c
index 7c26f8f565cb..47fbf1d1e557 100644
--- a/drivers/mtd/spi-nor/controllers/hisi-sfc.c
+++ b/drivers/mtd/spi-nor/controllers/hisi-sfc.c
@@ -399,8 +399,10 @@ static int hisi_spi_nor_register_all(struct hifmc_host *host)
 
 	for_each_available_child_of_node(dev->of_node, np) {
 		ret = hisi_spi_nor_register(np, host);
-		if (ret)
+		if (ret) {
+			of_node_put(np);
 			goto fail;
+		}
 
 		if (host->num_chip == HIFMC_MAX_CHIP_NUM) {
 			dev_warn(dev, "Flash device number exceeds the maximum chipselect number\n");
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `drivers/mtd/spi-nor/controllers/hisi-sfc.c`**
- A new line was added to the error handling section of the `hisi_spi_nor_register_all` function. Specifically, if the call to `hisi_spi_nor_register(np, host)` fails (i.e., `ret` is non-zero), the child node pointer `np` is now released using `of_node_put(np)` before the function exits with a failure status. This ensures that the reference to the child node is properly managed and prevents memory leaks.

### Relationships
- The modification addresses a potential memory management issue that could occur when the device registration fails. By adding the `of_node_put(np)` call, the patch ensures that the child node is properly released in the error path, which is crucial for maintaining the integrity of the device tree and preventing resource leaks. This change is directly related to the previous implementation that did not handle the child node correctly upon failure, as indicated by the Fixes tag referencing a specific commit.
